item.title: Gulf states postpone strait of Hormuz talks with Iran as Yemen conflict intensifies
item.description:
Twenty-five years after 9/11, the United States is again fighting a major war in the Middle East. Drop Site’s Ryan Grim and Murtaza Hussain speak with Vali Nasr, professor of international affairs and Middle East studies at Johns Hopkins SAIS and a former senior adviser in the Obama administration, and Rob Malley, a senior fellow at Yale’s Jackson School of Global Affairs, former U.S. special envoy for Iran, longtime Middle East peace negotiator, and head of the Middle East program at the International Crisis Group. The conversation covers Ansarallah’s advance in Yemen, the battle over the Strait of Hormuz, Iran and the US duel strategies of economic pressure, the future of U.S. military bases in the Gulf, the collapse of the JCPOA, Iran’s nuclear calculations, and whether Washington has learned the lessons of Iraq, Afghanistan and the broader post-9/11 wars. item.title: Kennedy Center board to propose new options for honoring Trump, according to court filing
item.description:
When President Donald Trump announced a takeover of the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts last year, he claimed to be fighting a specific sort of cultural rot at the Washington, D.C., institution. "We don't need woke at the Kennedy Center," he said in February 2025. "So I'll be there until such time as it gets to be running right." The president abandoned that in May 2026, after a federal judge ruled that the center was illegally renamed after Trump. Trump's remedy for a "woke" Kennedy Center was to replace one alleged strain of political capture with another. The center operates in a gray zone between the public and private sectors. Taxpayers fund building maintenance, operations, security, and repairs. Private donors and ticket sales, meanwhile, are the main source of money for programming. item.title: Russian strike on passenger train will not deter Ukraine’s backers, Nato chief says
item.description:
Mark Rutte says attack that narrowly missed Boris Johnson and David Petraeus shows Vladimir Putin’s desperation The head of Nato has said a Russian drone attack on a train close to Ukraine’s border with Poland would not deter Kyiv’s western backers. Mark Rutte said the strike on a passenger train showed how desperate Vladimir Putin had become. “He thinks that he can stops us from supporting Ukraine and that he can undermine our unity. item.title: Africa's richest man launches continent's biggest share sale
item.description:
The News Africa’s richest man Aliko Dangote tapped the opening gong this morning on the floor of the Lagos exchange to open Africa’s largest initial public offer. The $20 billion Dangote Refinery built on swamp land on the outskirts of Lagos becomes the fourth Dangote Industries subsidiary to go public in Nigeria. When the initial offer closes next month, the company will have raised more than $4 billion at about a $50 billion valuation, if demand matches the year-long buzz partly driven by the company’s pledge to pay dividends in US dollars.
